Fight with Insight II

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Young lives diverted from a life of crime through a novel boxing programme

Unique Selling Point:
Ten years on from the first insert on FIGHT WITH INSIGHT, we revisit Luke Lamprecht and the young men whose lives have been saved through the discipline of boxing at the Fight with Insight gym on the outskirts of the roughest parts of Johannesburg. Taking a glimpse behind the scenes of these young men's lives, we discover where they might have been if it hadn't been for the programme that teaches them the values of teamwork, consideration, self-control and healthy competition.

Summary:
Initially an offender diversion programme but now have realised prevention is better
Fight with Insight is a project of the Box Office Gym, which was started by Luke Lamprecht and Anton Gilmore in 2006. Anton, is an ex pro boxer, trainer and promoter, with over 20 years first-hand experience of the impact that boxing has in the lives of youth in the Southern Suburbs of Rosettenville. Luke has 25 years experience in the child protection and development field and works with many Non Profit Organisations. Anton and Luke are supported by Sheri Errington, a Research Psychologist with more than 10 years Non -Profit Monitoring and Evaluation experience. In 2014 Fight with Insight launched an open access boxing gym in the inner city of Johannesburg, in response to the needs of children living there.
Fight with Insight was established with the vision of creating a safe place for the children of Johannesburg, using boxing to teach them life skills that assist them in taking responsibility for claiming their rights. They aim to contribute positively to healthy lifestyles and sustainable communities for children.


Further information:
2017 was special year for Fight with Insight as the momentum of the club really gained traction. They currently have different segments now at the gym all delivering life assistance through boxing. From a fight perspective the club was very active taking part in 80 percent of the total fight .The children have won close to 70 percent of our fights. FWI Registered as a boxing club and has 83 fighter-one of the biggest clubs in Gauteng.

Autistic Boxing
Johannesburg School for Autism “Fight with Insight” has developed and delivers boxing classes for approximately 100 learners with Autism aged 10 - 21 years, as a part of their weekly physical education and occupational therapy programme. This programme has been running for 2 years, and has been observed by Occupational Therapists, Neurologists, Psychologists and Neurodevelopment specialists to have had a significant positive impact on the participants social, cognitive, emotional and physical development. Recognising the potential of this programme, and the expressed need for holistic health promotion amongst young people with Autism, Fight with Insight set up a project team, consisting of multi -disciplinary professionals (Psychologists, Psychiatrists, Neuro -developmentalists, Occupational Therapists, Physiologists, Social Workers, Design Experts and Researchers) to build out the Boxing - 4 -Autism programme, so it can be replicated anywhere in the world and scaled to support a much wider base of young people in the ASD community. We are currently sourcing funding to support the evidence development, design and implementation of the programme in other locations. Making comments
Mindfulness
Mindfulness The programme focuses on developing coordination and strength, discipline, enjoying the benefits of exercise, and experiencing a positive outlet for their anger, frustration, and energy. Within the programme, and usually at the end of each boxing session, I have used a combination of physical yoga postures and breathing exercises, in order to bring the participants into the awareness of their bodies and minds. Yogic breath exercises are used to connect to the self and develop introspection and awareness within the body. Often, sufferers of anxiety, stress, and psychological disorders experience a constant feeling of being outside of the body and mind - a feeling of disconnect. However, with the use of breath exercises and bodily observation one is able to come back into the sensations of the body and be present

Script:


V/O Ten years ago Carte Blanche took to the ring alongside NGO Fight with Insight, where we met child protection and development specialist Luke Lempracht ,as well as former world title champion Anton Gilmore.They ran a diversion programme for youth offenders in Johannesburg ,but Instead of using more conventional forms of therapy they opted for a less orthodox method ,using boxing as a way of remoulding negative behaviour.
Upsound Old Story : Luke lempracht approached me and said Anton these Kids have made mistakes, how are we going to help them? Put a program together where we get these kids back on track. In essence it’s a second chance.
Upsound Old Story: What’s interesting is that boxing because it is social contact … and it teaches discipline
V/O 10 years on Fight with Insight has expanded exponentially, making the programme available to a wider network of young people from the inner city.
Derek’s Questions: Look a lot seems to have happened since last we were with you.
Upsound : we’ve developed from the diversion program, we’ve developed an open access gym so that inner city children have a place where they can be fit, they can eat well and lifeskills
Upsound:we have social workers, we have therapists who come, we have audiology test-so we do the basic health screening and very importantly if children are poor, they don’t eat enough,so we have a big nutrition programme
Upsound:The right of passage I am giving them here is a pro social way to belong, as opposed to belonging to a gang. Boxing is the hook that brings young people here.
Link: Just like Rocky Balboa in the tough streets of Philadelphia ,most of the children here are from the tough inner city ,have always had their backs against the ropes -they’ve have had to fight ,scratch and claw for every inch in life.
V/O One youngsters who has toughened up for life in Hillbrow is 17 year old Jennifer Matibi.She lives with her mother Samukeliso Matibi in this one bedroom flat.
Upsound: Growing up in the inner city is really hard I won’t lie as a girl most of the things we see is prostitution most of our young ladies are being exposed to drugs and there’s a high rate of teenage pregnancy.


V/O Exposed to the dark side of city life, Jennifer lost her way. She spiralled out of control.
Jennifer’s mother
Upsound:Jennifer’s [Fix]behaviour was not right at all, whenever I went to work ,she would be alcohol with her friends, I would often find her very drunk.
V/O At the age of 12 she attempted suicide following an argument with her mother , she nearly lost her life and was hospitalised for three weeks.
I decided to drink all the pills I could find at home,I eventually passed out and woke up in hospital…
I decided to lie and said my mom used to abuse me, they wanted to take me away from my mom. One day she came into my ward. I could see the pain in her eyes,I saw what I was doing was really wrong.I decided to tell them I lied all along
V/O following her confession to social workers Jennifer was referred to Fight with Insight,where she made rapid progress.
V/O She even started a business making hair accessories using recycled materials and was chosen as one of the top young entrepreneurs in Gauteng by business incubator Beyond the lemonade Stand. Currently she runs Nirvana ,a support group for young women in the inner city.
Coach Anton:
Jennifer was a polite girl,educated, Shes come out of herself,she was very shy when she arrived…she’s just excelling school wise she had the ideals of becoming an entrepreneur, she’s doing very well
Jennifer’s mother
Since she started working with Fight with insight she started to change, Today she is a good child
Link: Violence, drugs, prostitution, many of the young people at fight with insight have been exposed to the dark side of city life, many never make it out and are caught in the cycle of poverty and crime.
I got into a lot of crime activities, like house break ins and robbing people,I also had to sell some illegal stuff
V/O Growing up 21 year old Lucky Mlakalaka Nhassambo was a troubled child, with no positive male role models , he was destined for a life of crime on streets of Hillbrow.
Upsound: growing up in the inner city I’ve always looked up to people who are not very good…gangsters…exactly. I had to do a lot of bad things, hurt to a lot of people.
V/O Initially joining Fight with Insight to improve his street fighting skills, Lucky met Luke and Anton who saw potential in him and took him under their wing.
Upsound:My coach set me down and said if you want to continue with this kind of life style , youre going to end up in two kind of places , either you go to prison or you’re going to die.That kinda clicked something in my head.
Upsound: My coaches are the awesomest coaches I have ever seen, the impact that they’ve played in our lives has been has been huge.
V/O Lucky managed to turn his life around and has become a role model for the younger children at Fight with Insight. Even though he has hung up his gloves, he dreams of becoming a top boxing coach. He recently earned his coaching certificate, a proud moment for his mother Miriam Mokoena.
Upsound:I was so happy he told me mommy now I have a certificate, I was happy.I don’t know,I don’t know what to say hes doing good things
V/O He is hoping to teach and inspire the next generation of fighters.
I actually see myself in some of the youngsters because some of the are actually trapped in an environment where they don’t know what to do… they are still asking themselves if stealing something is the right thing or not… I’m still trying to find ways to change that
Link: Pent up anger, frustration and fear many of the children here have been through trying times situations, they have overcome the odds. Instead of letting life knock them down, they’ve rolled with the punches and are determined to make a better future for themselves.
V/O One of the first youngsters to Join Fight with Insight, was 23 year old Reginald Magashoa from Yeoville who took the opportunity to change his life. He applied himself diligently and through his never give up attitude has earned the respect of both his coaches and his peers
Reggie has done really well se was in the initial programme…and studied himself up into a position of power and so hes doing well
I went there as a rehabilitation programme.Growing up in Yeoville… it’s not the safest place to grow up in …I was around bad people, there was a huge chance of me getting into trouble
V/OThrough Fight with insight Reginald was able to reclaim his confidence furthering his education and obtain a honours in Brand Strategy .He currently works as a researcher at a top financial institution,but boxing is still his first love.
Derek question Very much, at first it was something I did because I had to…it slowly became a part of me and I can’t imagine myself without me.
Derek question
No one enjoys taking punches( laughs), it comes with the sport,you learn to appreciate the punches
Derek Question
I had the chance to turn professional, its just that I needed to accomplish that goal of going to the Olympics
V/O While a lot of young men and women have been saved from a life of despair, many still fall through the cracks, but Fight with Insight is determined to land the final blow on poverty and crime in the inner city.
Upsound:We live in a city of limitless resources and we need to celebrate our victories and the hardest thing for me is to mourn actively for what I could not do


Promos:
V/O Using the discipline of Boxing to remould negative behaviour in young people NGO Fight with Insight is taking youth of Johannesburg of the streets and into the boxing ring
No one thinks that good kids come out of the city,its kind of like you survive the city, so children need to be resistant to the influence of the city… and in order to be resistant there needs to be a level where we give them the skills to resist the city. 15 sec: Violence, drugs, prostitution, many children in Johannesburg are exposed to the dark side of city Life,many never make it out and are caught in the cycle of poverty and crime, but NGO Fight with insight is hoping to change this one punch at a time.
15 sec: What started off as a diversion programme for offenders in Johannesburg, has grown into one of the biggest boxing clubs in Gauteng. Using boxing to keep young men and women from a life of crime,Fight with Insight is giving the youth in the inner city a fighting chance.
Violence, drugs, prostitution many children in Johannesburg are exposed to the dark side of city life and are caught in the cycle of poverty and crime,but NGO Fight with Insight is hoping to change this one punch at a time.
10 sec Using the discipline of boxing to impart life skills, Fight with Insight is changing the lives of young people in the inner city by taking them off the street and into the boxing ring.

This programme has been running for 2 years, and has been observed by Occupational Therapists, Neurologists, Psychologists and Neurodevelopment specialists to have had a significant positive impact on the participants social, cognitive, emotional and physical development. Recognising the potential of this programme, and the expressed need for holistic health promotion amongst young people with Autism, Fight with Insight set up a project team, consisting of multi -disciplinary professionals (Psychologists, Psychiatrists, Neuro -developmentalists, Occupational Therapists, Physiologists, Social Workers, Design Experts and Researchers) to build out the Boxing - 4 -Autism programme, so it can be replicated anywhere in the world and scaled to support a much wider base of young people in the ASD community. We are currently sourcing funding to support the evidence development, design and implementation of the programme in other locations. Making comments Mindfulness Mindfulness The programme focuses on developing coordination and strength, discipline, enjoying the benefits of exercise, and experiencing a positive outlet for their anger, frustration, and energy. Within the programme, and usually at the end of each boxing session, I have used a combination of physical yoga postures and breathing exercises, in order to bring the participants into the awareness of their bodies and minds. Yogic breath exercises are used to connect to the self and develop introspection and awareness within the body. Often, sufferers of anxiety, stress, and psychological disorders experience a constant feeling of being outside of the body and mind - a feeling of disconnect. However, with the use of breath exercises and bodily observation one is able to come back into the sensations of the body and be present
